messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: detected sustained p99 tail spikes on router LB affecting streaming responses across eu-* regions. SLOs breached for 00:08. Auto-mitigation attempted (fallback to v2-model) but tail persists. Alert group: #incidents paging.

jordan-oncall: acked. I'm on it — grabbing logs and current routing policy.

alex: seeing p95 ~ 420ms -> 820ms and p99 hitting 2.6s on streaming endpoints. Non-streaming generation p99 also elevated but less severe.
maria: any customer-facing errors? Support dashboard shows increased user timeouts for a handful of smaller customers in eu-west-1.
support-bot: Affected customers: cust-420 (prod), cust-171 (staging), cust-ops-sandbox. Support tickets auto-created.
jordan-oncall: copying top-level graphs: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/routers/latency?orgId=1&from=now-30m&to=now

samir: logs show a sudden spike in requests routed to shard 7 on lb-edge-eu1. Connection queues for that shard are growing, reuse ratio low.

emily: rough grep from router logs: ```
2026-03-14T18:05:12Z INFO route_assign shard=7 lb_policy=weight-based delta_policy=applied
2026-03-14T18:05:12Z WARN hot_shard_detected shard=7 qlen=312 p99=2.45s
2026-03-14T18:05:13Z INFO fallback_trigger shard=7 fallback_target=pool-eu-backup
```

jalex (typo correction): alex: ^ meant to say linking query id: q=abcd-1234 for tail spans.
jordan-oncall: initial hypothesis: policy delta pushed ~18:05 that skewed weight mapping to favor older hot GPU hosts in shard 7 causing head-of-line blocking and streaming stalls. Need to confirm config change.
maria: who rolled the lb-policy change? Any config PRs around 18:00?
alex: I see an operator tag from deploy-bot: "lb-policy-weights-v3" merged 2026-03-14T17:59:58Z by infra-ops.
samir: rolling back policy may be fastest mitigation. Options: revert config, drain shard 7, or steer traffic away via a shim rule. Which has least blast radius?
jordan-oncall: prefer steering traffic first (non-disruptive). Let's add a temporary route override to deprioritize shard 7 and send a percentage to eu-backup pools.
emily: I can apply a dynamic override. Command: ```
redwoodctl route override set --scope=eu --match='router:*' --policy='deprioritize:shard=7,send:pool=eu-backup,weight=70' --expires=10m
```

jordan-oncall: apply it now.
emily: applied. override id=ovr-20260314-1. Monitoring.

alex: immediate drop in qlen for shard 7 within 30s, p99 starting to tail down. Graphs updating.
maria: confirm customer impact window estimate so we can notify CS/ops.
support-bot: automated estimate: ~7-12 minutes of degraded experience for listed customers; retries increased by 3x. Tickets updated with mitigation note.
jordan-oncall: good. keep override for 10m and we will reassess. Also start draining shard 7 for full remediation. Samir, can you coordinate drain?
samir: starting drain: ```
redwoodctl shard drain --shard=7 --mode=graceful --timeout=5m
```

emily: drain started, current inflight connections 46 -> 12 -> 3.
jordan-oncall: once drained, we'll remove bad hosts from lb rotation and validate weight mapping. Also schedule a revert of the merge PR if it's the root cause.
alex: digging traces: many affected requests show a specific codepath in streaming multiplexer where a single slow host stalls the common KV cache access. That amplifies tail latency across multiplexed streams.
maria: interesting — so not pure traffic concentration; a host-level slowdown is amplifying rollback. Could be bad kernel patch or thermal issue on GPU host. Any host-level alarms?
samir: host metrics show elevated GPU memory pressure and occasional OOM kills on process 'llm-runtime' around that time on host eu-edge-7-3.
jordan-oncall: mark host eu-edge-7-3 as quarantined. Command: ```
infractl host quarantine --host=eu-edge-7-3 --reason='runtime oom spike, amplifying tail'
```
emily: quarantined. Traffic to that host dropped to zero. Monitoring p99: now back to ~480ms. p95 stable ~380ms.

alex: looks like combo: weight mapping change + one degraded host = cascading tail. Both must be addressed.
maria: action list for post-incident: revert lb-policy-weights-v3 PR, full host health postmortem, add an automated detection for skew when single-shard qlen > 200, update canary checks to include streaming latency on small sample of EU traffic.
jordan-oncall: agreed. Immediate next steps: 1) keep override until policy revert, 2) drain & reprovision hosts in shard 7, 3) open postmortem ticket and notify affected customers with timeline.
support-bot: Notifying CS and sending templated customer communication draft to #customer-success.

emily: rolling revert PR now. ```
git revert -m 1 commit:lb-policy-weights-v3
push && deploy
```

alex: revert merged and deployed to staging, and then to eu region.
jordan-oncall: monitoring for 5m after revert. If stable, we'll remove the override.
emily: metrics show steady improvement; p99 trending below SLO threshold.
maria: final check: any data loss or request failures? Logs show increased timeouts but no 5xxs spike. Cache hits unaffected.
support-bot: closing immediate customer-impact tickets with "mitigated" tag and adding postmortem link when available.
jordan-oncall: thanks team. reopening if anything recurs. Postmortem owner: maria. Follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-15 10:00 UTC. :white_check_mark:
